svg.text: Глава 6 · Линии связи
Олифер, 7-е изд. · RAG p0183:c01–p0214:c01 · PDF 183–214 · printed 182–213
1 · What is the physical line?
Link → adjacent nodes · Channel → portion of link capacity · Circuit → end-to-end path
DTE creates/consumes data · DCE terminates line and performs PHY signaling
Guided media → copper / fiber · Unguided media → radio (covered later in book)
Analog line → amplification/FDM example · Digital line → regeneration/TDM example
Physical link can include intermediate amplifiers / regenerators / primary-network equipment
2 · Signal and spectrum
Sinusoid parameters → amplitude · period/frequency · phase · wavelength
Fourier → periodic signal as sum of harmonics
Significant harmonics define practical spectrum width
Line frequency response changes amplitude/phase by frequency
Spectrum view lets engineer predict waveform distortion through a medium
3 · Power, attenuation, noise
Attenuation → change of signal power across line
dB → ratio · dBm → absolute power referenced to fixed level
Link budget → transmitter level − losses + gains vs receiver sensitivity
Noise/SNR + NEXT/FEXT + BER describe recognition risk
Source attenuation sign convention is not fully consistent → state convention explicitly
Do not copy OCR-damaged power-unit examples literally
4 · Bandwidth and capacity
Bandwidth → frequency interval in Hz with acceptable attenuation
Capacity → maximum bit/s for line + chosen physical coding/protocol
Baud → signal-state changes per second · not automatically bit/s
More states can carry more bits/symbol, but noise limits distinguishability
Shannon → bandwidth + SNR · Nyquist → bandwidth + signal states
Theoretical limit ≠ negotiated production PHY rate
5 · Copper media
Twisted pair → twisting reduces external/mutual interference
STP adds electromagnetic shielding · UTP relies primarily on twisting
Cable category constrains frequency/crosstalk characteristics for standards
Coax → center conductor + dielectric + outer conductor/shield
Twinax example → two internal conductors for short high-rate links
Real deployment limits require exact cable/standard revision
6 · Fiber media
SMF → small core · low attenuation · long/high-rate links
MMF → wider core · easier coupling · modal effects
LED / laser sources depend on fiber/use case
Impairments → attenuation · chromatic dispersion · PMD · nonlinear effects
Optical links avoid most external EM interference, not all physical limits
7 · Structured cabling as operational architecture
Horizontal subsystem → floor/user outlets · Vertical subsystem → floor closets to building room
Campus subsystem → building interconnect · standard panels/connectors make moves/adds/changes predictable
No executable CLI is supplied by the chapter; physical rollback must preserve original patching/media.
Chapter 7 starts at p0215:c01 · reading state unchanged · source extraction findings recorded separately.
